Thanks Marissa — quick review from tax/procurement: because the bank letter lists BlueOak Holdings, LLC (parent) while the W-9 is BlueOak Software, Inc., we need one of the following: a) corrected bank letter reflecting BlueOak Software, Inc.; b) a stamped bank letter that lists both the parent and the subsidiary with a clear line showing the account belongs to the subsidiary; or c) a government document (state filing) showing the DBA relationship plus an addendum signed by an authorized signer confirming the account mapping.

If BlueOak can provide (a) or (b) we can proceed without legal sign-off. If they can only provide (c), loop Legal for final approval — that will add 2–3 business days.

Ethan — can you ask your bank for a letter that includes the subsidiary name exactly as shown on the W-9? If not, let us know and we will open the legal review path. Also confirm whether the EIN on the bank letter and the W-9 match — I did a quick check and they appear the same, which is good.
